cppDE reaches a steady state in two ways: by integrating the ODE until the flow stops
(`rootfunc = "equilibrate"`), with sensitivities, or by solving $f(x, p) = 0$ directly with
[`ptc()`](../reference/ptc.html), under conservation laws.

```{r library}
library(cppDE)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Model definition

The decay chain with production `k0` of $A$ has the steady state $A = k_0/k_1$, $B = k_0/k_2$.
`rootfunc` of [`cppODE()`](../reference/cppODE.html) ends the integration: `"equilibrate"` at
steady state, a vector of expressions at the first zero of any of them. `ptc()` takes a
[`cppFUN()`](../reference/cppFUN.html) object with forward derivatives, here the right-hand sides
of an enzyme $E + S \rightleftharpoons ES \to E + P$ with $P \to S$, and of a bistable switch.

```{r models}
eqns  <- c(A = "k0 - k1*A", B = "k1*A - k2*B")
parms <- c(A = 1, B = 0, k0 = 1, k1 = 0.5, k2 = 0.2)

steady <- cppODE(eqns, rootfunc = "equilibrate", modelname = "g5_steady", compile = FALSE)
cross  <- cppODE(eqns, rootfunc = "A - B", modelname = "g5_cross", compile = FALSE)

enzyme <- c(E  = "-kon*E*S + (koff + kcat)*ES",
            S  = "-kon*E*S + koff*ES + kback*P",
            ES = " kon*E*S - (koff + kcat)*ES",
            P  = " kcat*ES - kback*P")
enz <- cppFUN(enzyme, variables = names(enzyme),
              parameters = c("kon", "koff", "kcat", "kback"), modelname = "g5_enzyme")
switch1 <- cppFUN(c(x = "a + b*x^2/(1 + x^2) - x"), variables = "x",
                  parameters = c("a", "b"), modelname = "g5_switch")

compile(steady, cross, enz, switch1, output = "guide5", cores = 2)
```

## Integration to steady state

Under `rootfunc = "equilibrate"`, [`solveODE()`](../reference/solveODE.html) stops once every
$|\mathrm{d}x_i/\mathrm{d}t| \le \mathtt{roottol}\, |x_i| + \mathtt{abstol}$, on the
sensitivities as well. The last time of `times` bounds the integration; the last row of the
result is the steady state with sensitivities.

```{r equilibrate}
outQ <- solveODE(steady, c(0, 1e4), parms, abstol = 1e-10, reltol = 1e-10, roottol = 1e-10)
n <- length(outQ$time)
outQ$time[n]
outQ$variable[n, ]
outQ$tangent[n, , ]
```

$\partial A/\partial k_0 = 1/k_1 = 2$ and $\partial B/\partial k_2 = -k_0/k_2^2 = -25$; the
derivatives in the initial values vanish. A smaller `roottol` integrates longer and leaves a
smaller residual in each derivative.

## Termination root

An expression as `rootfunc` stops at the first zero crossing, here where $A$ and $B$ meet. The
output ends at the crossing time.

```{r cross}
outX <- solveODE(cross, seq(0, 10, by = 0.1), parms)
tail(outX$time, 2)
tail(outX$variable, 1)
```

## Pseudo-transient continuation

`ptc()` solves $f(x, p) = 0$ for the variables `solve`, paired with the outputs `rows`, by
pseudo-transient continuation: implicit Euler steps on $\dot x = f$ far from the root, Newton
steps near it ([methods](methods-ptc.html)). The enzyme conserves $E + ES$ and $S + ES + P$, so the
Jacobian is singular and the steady state is fixed by the totals: `C` holds the conservation laws
as rows, columns named by the solved variables, and `total` the right-hand side of
$C x = \mathtt{total}$.

```{r ptc}
C <- rbind(Etot = c(E = 1, S = 0, ES = 1, P = 0),
           Stot = c(E = 0, S = 1, ES = 1, P = 1))
pe <- c(kon = 1, koff = 0.5, kcat = 0.3, kback = 0.1)
ss <- ptc(enz, x = c(E = 1, S = 1, ES = 1, P = 1), parms = pe, C = C, total = c(1, 10))
ss$x
c(converged = ss$converged, iterations = ss$iterations)
ss$message
drop(C %*% ss$x)
do.call(enz$func, c(as.list(ss$x), as.list(pe)))
```

Variables outside `solve` keep the values of `x`. With the substrate clamped, the remaining
variables are solved with the enzyme total alone.

```{r ptc-solve}
ptc(enz, x = c(E = 1, S = 2, ES = 1, P = 1), parms = pe, solve = c("E", "ES", "P"),
    C = rbind(Etot = c(E = 1, ES = 1, P = 0)), total = 1)$x
```

## Stability of the steady state

With `flow = TRUE` (default), the outputs are the right-hand side of an ODE and `ptc()` returns a
stable steady state: the real part of every Jacobian eigenvalue on the kernel of `C` is
non-positive ([stability test](methods-ptc.html#stability)). From an unstable root the search
continues along the unstable direction. `flow = FALSE` takes plain equations and returns any
regular root. The switch has a stable root on each side of an unstable one, near
$x = 0.41$ for $a = 0.05$, $b = 2.5$.

```{r stability, fig.height = 3}
ps <- c(a = 0.05, b = 2.5)
sapply(c(0.40, 0.42), function(x0) c(
  start  = x0,
  flow   = ptc(switch1, x = c(x = x0), parms = ps)$x,
  noFlow = ptc(switch1, x = c(x = x0), parms = ps, flow = FALSE)$x))

xs <- seq(0, 2.5, by = 0.01)
ggplot(data.frame(x = xs, f = switch1$func(x = xs, a = 0.05, b = 2.5)[, "x"]), aes(x, f)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey60") +
  geom_line() +
  labs(y = "dx/dt")
```

`controls = list(stability = FALSE)` accepts any root of the flow; `stabilityTol` accepts a root
whose leading eigenvalue is at most this positive value, as near a Hopf bifurcation.
`positive = TRUE` (default) keeps the solved variables positive; they must start positive.

```{r stability-off}
ptc(switch1, x = c(x = 0.42), parms = ps, controls = list(stability = FALSE))$x
```

## Tolerances of ptc()

`controls` of `ptc()` sets the iteration:

| control | default | meaning |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `reltol` | `1e-10` | residual of each row relative to the turnover, the sum of the rates that cancel in it |
| `abstol` | `1e-14` | absolute floor, relative to the largest Jacobian entry of the row |
| `flowTol` | `1` | relative local error of a pseudo-time step |
| `maxit` | `400` | iterations of one descent |
| `dtInit` | `1e-2` | first pseudo-time step, relative to the fastest rate under `flow = TRUE` |
| `zmax` | `5` | largest change of the logarithm of a variable per step |
| `stability` | `TRUE` | require a stable root under `flow = TRUE` |
| `stabilityTol` | `0` | largest leading eigenvalue counted as stable |

After convergence, Newton steps bring each variable to within `reltol * (abs(x) + abstol)` of the
root. The result depends on the start, the parameters and the controls only, so equal inputs
return the same root to the last digit.

```{r tolerances}
sapply(c(1e-4, 1e-10), function(tol) {
  r <- ptc(enz, x = c(E = 1, S = 1, ES = 1, P = 1), parms = pe, C = C, total = c(1, 10),
           controls = list(reltol = tol))
  c(reltol = tol, iterations = r$iterations, deltaES = r$x[["ES"]] - ss$x[["ES"]])
})
```

`ptc()` returns the steady state without derivatives. dMod2 calls the same solver from C++ for the
steady states of `Pimpl()`, with sensitivities by the implicit function theorem.
